commits.summary: application-core objects O1: an ordinary receiver made by its constructor in the regression and property checks (verification pending)
commits.body:
An instance method of a class that is not a record of primitive components was refused by both equivalence and prove. construction::receiver now makes such a receiver exactly as an object parameter is made (equivalence::made_of, the one usable constructor from primitive leaves and objects made so in turn), named this. In equivalence both versions' receivers must be made the same way; their fields are compared after the call, and this is a new root of the identity relations (harness::Root::Receiver). In prove the target is called on its receiver (invokevirtual) and the assumption, the assertion and the throws clauses read this.f. A receiver outside that is refused by name: a constructor argument that is an array, a String or a dependency says the objects stream builds it; several constructors, a superclass, a cycle, --nullable this, --before-arguments and a correspondence about the receiver are named boundaries.

Verified inline on the native engine with no JBMC: the integration contract's O1 (the throttle's allows verified after construction, one-short refuted and replayed), and five tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs (a receiver's mutation refuted on field:this and run on a JVM, a receiver returned as a copy refuted on identity with this, properties over this.f proved and refuted, the refusals, and cache invalidation by the receiver's constructor). The lib tests and the heap, foundations, compare, effects, application_core, observations, alignment and summaries suites pass. Job 20261108-045000-application-core-objects-o1-lib-tests-in runs lib/tests/integration.rs (JBMC) and examples 190-196, whose kernels recorded Quote#quantity as unresolved for being an instance method.

Found on the way, and not fixed here because proof_cache.rs is the reuse stream's: the regression cache's key doesn't root a version's closure at inner objects' constructors, so a build that changes only an inner constructor reuses another build's proof. That is an unsound hit, which predates this wave. Its reproducer is an ignored test, an_inner_objects_constructor_is_part_of_the_cached_claim, and the stream brief's Progress records it for the reuse stream and the main brief's for-review list.

commits.summary: application-core objects O1 and O3: a construction plan chooses the constructor, and a setup sequence of one or two calls is checked and replayed as a whole history
commits.body:
equivalence --plan, prove --plan and a planned claim (spec::heap::check) now make their inputs by the plan: construction::root builds each root by the constructor descriptor its node names, which is how one of several constructors is chosen. construction::setup_calls gives one or two void calls on the receiver, which the regression harness calls in both versions before the target. A setup call that throws ends that version's history, and its exception, a category of its step's own, is the outcome compared, so an input one version's setup rejects is a difference and is never dropped. The property harness skips such a history, as it skips a rejected construction. The interpreter replay runs the history, the JVM run gets it by running the harness, and the witness reads 'allows(this=new Throttle(...), n=...), after the setup this.take(setup.0.n=...)'. The statement gains the setup assumption and setupCalls; a planned claim's result names its label and restrictions; the domain gate compares a plan's classes with the claim's. What a plan can't make yet is refused by its stream's name: arrays, nullable or shared nodes, factories, dependencies, adapted values, setup calls that return a value, more than two setup calls, plans that differ between versions. A setup claim runs uncached (its key wouldn't root the setup methods), and prove --cache --plan is refused (the property key doesn't read the plan).

Verified inline, native engine and no JBMC: four new tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. (1) O3 on the frozen throttle claims, with only their allocation bound raised to 1: after-setup is verified with no setup, labelled for that domain, and refuted after one take, the whole history in the witness and run on a JVM; one-short is refuted and after verified under both claims. (2) A plan choosing one of Window's two constructors, verified and refuted, with a missing constructor and a misnamed leaf refused. (3) A setup rejection in one version only, refuted on exception. (4) prove over the states one setup call reaches. The lib tests, heap (its Phase 0 placeholder test for a planned domain now checks the plan instead), foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill all pass.

Found, and recorded for the coordinator under the brief's Progress: the frozen throttle claims bound allocations at 0, while allows and take each allocate the IllegalArgumentException they throw. Now that plans are checked, the allocation gate counts it, so the contract's O3 (tests/application_core.rs) is unresolved where expected.json says verified or refuted, and the integration check fails on O3 until the fixture is corrected. The gate is left as it is. Interface requests to reuse (root setup methods in the regression key; read the plan in the property key and in spec::cache::key) and to the coordinator (a setup field in witness::Call and its stored form; a plan input for compare) are recorded too. No new job: the harness changes apply only to layouts with setup calls, which no example or JBMC test has; the pending job 20261108-045000-application-core-objects-o1-lib-tests-in still covers the integration tests and examples 190-196.

commits.summary: application-core objects O1 and O2: a constructor may take a bounded primitive array, kept apart between the versions, and a leaked defensive copy is refuted
commits.body:
A construction's leaves are now primitives or arrays of integral or boolean elements (harness::is_leaf), with a plan or without one (equivalence::made_of), so a receiver or parameter such as Buffer(int[] data) needs no adapter of the application's. The previous version's object is made from the harness's copy of the array, so the two versions' heaps are apart, while within a version the object and the caller share the array the caller passed. The caller's array is compared after the call (array:this.data), in the harness and in the interpreter replay. The domain says each array of the construction is bounded, not null and its own, and construction::stated_bounds states the array bound, which the shared Domain::has_arrays doesn't see for an array inside an object. A plan's array values are roots or constructor arguments; their max_length must equal the check's array bound, and a null array or one value given at two paths is refused by name. A property's expressions still can't read an object's array field, refused by name as before.

Verified inline (native engine, no JBMC), with three new tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. A Buffer receiver: total rewritten is verified and a defect refuted and run on a JVM; a rewrite of bump, which writes into the receiver's own array, is verified, which it wouldn't be if both versions shared the array; prove verifies size() <= 3 and refutes total() >= 0. O2's negative control: a constructor that keeps the caller's array where the previous version copied it is refuted on array:this.data alone, the receivers' fields agreeing, replayed on a JVM. A plan's array leaf is checked, and a mismatched bound and a null array are refused. The lib tests and every inline suite pass, except the contract's O3, which still fails on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound recorded in the previous commit. No job: apart from the quote fixture's QuoteRequest, whose String argument is still refused, no example or fixture class has a constructor that takes a primitive array, so no example's result changes.

commits.summary: application-core objects O2: a plan's root may be null or one of other roots' objects, one node at two roots is one object, and two parameters that were one object becoming distinct is refuted
commits.body:
A construction plan's root node may now be null (nullable) or one of the objects of other roots (same_as), each a boolean flag of the harness made as --nullable and --may-alias make it, and one node at two roots is one object, always, with no flag: harness::Choice::always, set by Layout::share and honoured by both harnesses' bytecode and source, by Layout::made (so the witness, the interpreter replay and the JVM run of the harness), and by the domain ('b: the same object as a'). Both versions' plans must make the same choices, so that their identity relations start alike. Inside a nested object a choice or a shared node stays refused by name, as do a shared node with a choice besides, a same_as naming no root's node, and a nullable receiver.

Verified inline on the native engine without JBMC: new unit tests in construction and harness, and four tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. The negative control of O2: a rewrite of twice(a, b) that keeps its first read of b is verified over two nodes and refuted over one node and over a same_as choice, the witness naming b as the same object as a, replayed in the interpreter and run on a JVM. Also: identity of the result with a shared node, a nullable root refuting a dropped null check, and a property over a shared node. The lib tests (228) and the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill pass; application_core passes except O3, which still waits on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound recorded for the coordinator in the brief's Progress. No job: no example or JBMC test has a plan with a shared node.

commits.body: The integration check of 05:36 stopped at the merge on a 4-sided conflict in lib/README.md (and in the generated llm-dlc/README.md, index.json and traces files, which are sync.py's and wait for the merge). This stream's four paragraphs (an ordinary receiver; a construction plan and a setup sequence; a plan's choices and shared nodes; arrays a constructor takes) sat right after the application-core paragraph of 'The foundations IR', where reuse adds too. They move, unchanged, to the end of 'How a regression proof works', where no other stream adds, so the README's additions merge as their union. Verified with the skill suite, which reads the README. Progress records it, and a non-additive README edit for the merge: Limits still says property proofs are over static methods only, which O1's receiver made out of date.

commits.summary: application-core objects O2: a constructor or setup call that writes a static field is refused by name, the negative control of unsupported side effects in a constructor
commits.body:
construction::side_effect finds a write to a static field in a constructor or in an application method it reaches (purity's walk, of which only that violation counts). Before, such a constructor was taken as it is, and since the checks make each object from the classes' initial state, a verdict over it was about the first object made only. It is now refused by name wherever a check makes an object: equivalence::made_of (receivers and parameters and their inner objects, in both versions and in prove), a plan's node, and a setup call, whose static write is outside every observation. The regression check's previous-version parameter now gives the reason instead of only 'not a record'. JDK calls with effects (System.out, clocks) were and stay refused by the engines. lib/README.md has a paragraph for it.

Verified inline (native, no JBMC): tests/application_core_objects.rs's o2_a_constructors_side_effect_outside_its_object_is_refused_by_name covers each refusal, System.out, and a constructor that reads a constant and writes its own field through a method, still verified. 17 pass and 1 ignored there. The lib tests (228) and the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill pass; application_core passes except O3, which still waits on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound (the coordinator's fixture finding in Progress). No job: no example or fixture constructor writes a static field. Found for the for-review list: a regression check doesn't observe the target's own static writes, and the README doesn't say so.

commits.summary: application-core objects O2: an input only one version's constructors accept is a difference, the negative control of a narrower new constructor under an anchored domain (verification pending)
commits.body:
Before, the regression harness skipped every input a constructor of either version rejected, so a new constructor that rejects inputs the old one accepted (step < 2 where it was step < 1) silently shrank the claim to the inputs both accept: such a change was verified, under a plain regression check and under the frozen throttle claim whose receiver is anchored by identity. Now the harness (lib/src/harness/mod.rs) makes the new version's objects, then the previous version's, in handler regions of their own, and compares their admission (Layout::compares_admission): an input both versions reject is skipped as before; one that only one version's constructors reject, narrower or wider, is a difference refuted on the exception, with a witness whose rejecting version throws in its constructor, replayed in the interpreter and run on a JVM. It applies where every object is made in both versions with the same shape; objects made through a correspondence's input equations, or only in the new version (--before-arguments), keep the old rule and its stated assumption. The constructible assumption text says which rule a check had, from a block marked for this stream in the shared statement.rs. Under a claim that does not require the exception, such a witness gives unresolved, never verified.

Verified inline on the native engine without JBMC: the new test in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs failed before (verified) and passes now; the lib tests (228) and the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill pass; application_core passes except O3, the known fixture allocation bound for the coordinator. Two harness unit tests and tests/conformance.rs's caveat text were updated to the new harness shape and the stricter rule. The JBMC integration tests and examples 126-131, 134-137, 150-152 and 190-196, whose harness bytecode changes shape, are job 20261108-063512-application-core-objects-o2-the-regressi.

For the merge: lib/README.md's How a regression proof works still says that an input a constructor of either version rejects is outside the statement; the new paragraph overrides it, since a stream only adds to the README. The brief is otherwise current.

commits.summary: application-core objects O2: a shrunk witness is the same failure as the one found, replayed before it is accepted (verification pending)
commits.body:
The shrinker's oracle was the generated harness alone, which accepts any failure, so a witness of one difference could shrink into a witness of another and be reported as the input found, shrunk. Reproducer (lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs, o2_a_shrunk_witness_reproduces_the_same_failure, failing before in both halves): a receiver's field difference found at add(this=new Counter(20), n=4) shrank to new Counter(1), where only the new constructor rejects the step, a difference on the exception; in prove, a violated assertion at new Counter(20) shrank into an IllegalStateException thrown at step 2. Now witness::shrink_in_harness_keeping takes a same-failure predicate, asked of every candidate the harness refutes: a regression check accepts a candidate whose two replays differ in exactly the observations the found input differs in, and a property check one where the same throws clause applies and the same exception class is thrown, or the method returns normally. Both shrink to new Counter(3) with the original failure, run on a JVM. The unchecked shrink_in_harness, which nothing called, is removed. A shrunk recipe stays legal by construction (the harness's own domain and admission rule, a plan's choice flags kept, no longer or null array); the doc and a new lib/README.md paragraph say so.

Verified inline (native engine, no JBMC): the stream's test file (19 pass, 1 ignored), the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill, and application_core except O3, the frozen throttle fixture's allocation bound recorded for the coordinator. The lib tests pass except a load-dependent timing test in the values stream's bmc/bits.rs, which passed alone 3 of 3, recorded under Progress. Also records that O1's job 20261108-045000 passed, and the 06:36 integration report, whose merge conflicts only in sync.py's generated files.

Job 20261108-064305-application-core-objects-o2-a-shrunk-wit: lib/tests/integration.rs under JBMC, whose tests assert particular shrunk witnesses.

commits.summary: application-core objects O2: every constructor and setup method that makes a check's inputs is listed as a claim root, for the reuse stream's key
commits.body:
harness::Layout::construction_roots gives, for each version, every method the harness calls to make the inputs besides the target: each object's constructor (inner objects' and a plan's chosen descriptor included), then the setup calls on that version's receiver class, in order and each once, the previous version's under its own build's names. The regression check's identical-bytecode shortcut now takes its roots from it (the same set as before). The proof cache's regression key (proof_cache.rs, the reuse stream's file) still roots only the target and the constructors, so a claim with a setup sequence keeps running uncached; the interface request under the brief's Progress asks reuse to root Regression::claim at construction_roots, after which this stream drops the guard at the merge.

Verified inline (native, no JBMC): a harness unit test of the roots, and tests/application_core_objects.rs's o2_a_setup_methods_edit_alone_is_another_claim_never_reused, where an edit of only the setup method add misses the cache and is refuted with its whole history, run on a JVM. With the uncached guard switched off it fails (the stale verified is reused); with the key rooted at construction_roots as well, tried in the working copy and reverted, it passes, as do the receiver-constructor cache test and the ignored inner-constructor one. Lib tests 229 of 229; the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill pass; application_core passes except O3, the frozen fixture's allocation bound already recorded for the coordinator. No job: no proof changes.

commits.body:
Jobs 20261108-063512-… and 20261108-064305-… both failed on one test only, a_method_of_a_record_is_proved_on_its_components, whose verdict, domain and 'behaves as before' held: it asserted the statement text of the single construction region that O2's comparison of constructor admission (d7330651) replaced with one region per version. commits.summary: application-core objects O2: a replay that cannot run one version reproduces nothing, and its witness is run on a JVM (verification pending)
commits.body:
The main brief's Phase 0 finding on VF-015's step 4: a regression witness whose new version the interpreter could not replay ('String.format depends on the default locale') was reported refuted and replay.reproduced true, an unknown outcome counting as a difference. A native reproducer (tests/application_core_objects.rs, o2_a_replay_that_cannot_run_one_version_is_no_reproduction, failing before) shows it twice under --gaps assume: a new version that throws with a message from String.formatted, refuted by the interpreter's half a replay; and a false refutation, where the checker's approximation of a formatted string's toString (a new object) took a path the JVM never takes (the JVM's String.toString returns the string itself), reported reproduced with after '<could not replay: ...>'. The property check had the same hole.

Now witness::differences names no difference where either replay could not run its version, and equivalence and prove run such a witness on a JVM, with or without contracts (before, only a witness through a contract was): a violation where the harness fails there (replay.by jvm, the differences the JVM's own, from each version run alone for static methods of plain parameters, otherwise none, which leaves a heap claim unresolved); unverifiable where the JVM finds the versions agreeing, the property holding, or cannot run it. unreproduced_cause names the gaps assumed under --gaps assume, and the proof line no longer mentions contracts a run did not apply. lib/README.md has a paragraph for it.

Verified inline (native, no JBMC): the reproducer (regression and property, each a real throw refuted on a JVM and a false refutation now unverifiable), the witness unit test a_replay_that_could_not_run_one_version_differs_in_nothing, the lib tests (230), 21 passing and 1 ignored in the stream's file, and the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill. application_core passes except O3, which still waits on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound (the coordinator's).
